subject: HSClinic pilot - data residency carveouts and subprocessor gating
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@hscliniccare.org>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hscliniccare.org>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot inquiry - residency & subprocessors

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — our clinical ops team is excited about the latency improvements. Before we proceed to a short pilot, we need to confirm a couple of items for the security review: 1) can Redwood commit to US-only residency for PHI during the pilot, and 2) we need a list of subprocessors and their regions (we will surface any non-US subprocessors to our DPO).

Can you share a redline-friendly DPA and a current subprocessor registry? We’re aiming for a minimal-scope pilot processing de-identified and limited PHI fields, but the CISO wants confirmation up front.

Best,
Elena Torres
Director, Clinical Ops
HSClinic Care Network

Attachment: pilot-data-map.xlsx (referenced, not included in this thread)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@hscliniccare.org>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot inquiry - residency & subprocessors

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and glad the demo was helpful.

Two quick answers up front: we can run a pilot scoped to US-only residency by configuring a US-only routing policy on your account, and we maintain a subprocessor registry (with region metadata) that we can share. I’m attaching an initial DPA draft and a spreadsheet listing current subprocessors and locations — note that some infra providers operate globally but we can restrict processing to US regions for this pilot.

High-level asks from our side to make the pilot smooth:
- Confirm the pilot data schema and expected daily request volume (helps us pick a dedicated pool vs hosted routing).
- If you have a preferred KMS or need customer-controlled keys, flag that now — we support Bring Your Own Key for Dedicated/private deployments.

Irene and Monica — looping you in for the subprocessor/residency gating details and to advise on contract redlines.

Thanks,

Logan Wright
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261001_Redwood_DPA_draft_v0.9.pdf, hsclinic_subprocessor_request.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot inquiry - residency & subprocessors

Logan — reviewed Elena's asks and our DPA draft. Quick notes for internal alignment:

1) Residency gating: We can enforce US-only processing by tagging the HSClinic account and applying a policy that rejects non-US worker allocations. This is a configuration control and does not require a contractual residency addendum during a time-limited pilot, but if they want a contractual residency clause, Legal will need to add a residency warranty plus limited audit right.

2) Subprocessors: Current registry has three categories — infra (cloud VMs), telemetry/monitoring, and third-party embeddings/collation services. For PHI scenarios we always recommend: a) exclude any optional downstream aggregators (we can disable telemetry forwarding), and b) offer to run embeddings on Dedicated or in their VPC to avoid third-party embedding providers.

3) Export controls / transfers: Our default DPA references EU-US transfer mechanisms; for US-only pilot this is less relevant, but the CISO may still ask about cross-border backups (we do encrypted backups to multi-region storage by default). We can scope backups to US regions for the pilot.

I’ll draft a short addendum language for the DPA restricting processing to US regions for the pilot period and enumerating subprocessors that will remain active. Monica — can you confirm if we can provide a limited audit snapshot (S3 manifest) rather than a full audit for the pilot?

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <dpark@hscliniccare.org>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@hscliniccare.org>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot inquiry - residency & subprocessors

Thanks, team. A couple of CISO clarifications before procurement moves forward:
- We need explicit confirmation that no UK/EEA data plane workers will be involved in request processing for the pilot.
- If backups are kept in multi-region storage, can you provide guaranteed geo-restriction during the pilot or a written operational control describing how backups are scoped?
- For subprocessors: please call out any monitoring agents that collect logs with user-level identifiers. We can accept a limited-scope access for compliance review (S3 manifest + sample log slice).

If Redwood can provide a one-page operational summary addressing these three items and a redline-capable DPA, we’ll be able to route to procurement/POL within the week.

-Daniel
Daniel Park
CISO, HSClinic Care Network

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@hscliniccare.org>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@hscliniccare.org>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot inquiry - residency & subprocessors

Daniel — thanks for the clear asks. Deliverables and next steps:

1) Operational summary: attached is a one-page ops snapshot that confirms US-only request routing, US-bound backups for the pilot, and the ability to disable optional telemetry agents.
2) Subprocessor detail: the attached spreadsheet marks any monitoring/logging agents that store user-level identifiers; for the pilot we will disable non-essential telemetry and offer Dedicated or VPC hosting so embeddings/third-party collators are not used.
3) DPA redline: we’ve uploaded a redline-friendly DPA and flagged two optional clauses — residency warranty (for procurement) and limited audit snapshot (S3 manifest + sample logs). If you want language tweaks, Legal (Irene) can accept tracked redlines.

Can we schedule a 30-minute ops walk-through on Thursday 2026-10-08 or Friday 2026-10-09 to confirm the exact schema and the daily volume so we can size the pool? I’m available 9–11am PT both days.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Logan Wright
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261007_Redwood_ops_snapshot_onepager.pdf, 20261001_Redwood_DPA_draft_v0.9.pdf, hsclinic_subprocessor_request.xlsx
